newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Post/Telstra may have bank role - Costello.
newsitem.headline: Australia Post/Telstra may have bank role - Costello.

text.p: The Australian government's telecoms group Telstra Corp and its mail and parcel delivery group Australia Post may have a role in an expanded financial services sector, national Treasurer Peter Costello said on Sunday.

Costello, asked about the government's response to the Wallis Inquiry's report on the financial system, said the two organisations could provide banking and other services to compete with the established banks, especially in Australia's regional areas, as both had branch networks in place.
"I think Australia Post could get increasingly into financial services," he said during an interview on the Nine Network's Business Sunday programme.
"I think Telstra could become a major player in relation to financial services."

Costello, who will respond in detail to the Wallis recommendations after the May 13 national budget is handed down, said Australia Post already provided some forms of transaction services such as payment of bills and the provision of money orders.
"One of the things I hope they are looking at and I'm certainly suggesting that they look at increasingly is upping the range of financial services that they offer.
"I think it would be a very exciting prospect, particularly in regional Australia."

While the government plans to float one-third of Telstra towards the end of calendar 1997, raising more than A$8 billion, Costello said the government did not have any plans to privatise Australia Post.

The Wallis Inquiry, led by Melbourne businessman Stan Wallis, finished its report last month. Costello released the report last Wednesday and broadly supported its calls for greater competition in the financial services sector.

However, Costello went against the deregulatory theme of the report by saying Australia's big four banks would not be able to merge with each other until the nation had a more competitive banking system in place for the small business sector.
